newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close choppy day lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close choppy day lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished a choppy day mixed, as Standard & Poor's 500s swung wildly on little fresh news, traders and analysts said.
"You had a combination of position-squaring and bargain-hunting, and that's why there was a push-and-pull all day," said Kurt Schultz, an analyst at Refco Inc.
"All in all, it was a directionless kind of day," he said.

Once again, traders pointed to declines in the U.S. bond market for the soft tone in S&Ps. March T-bonds' break through the lower end of a 2-1/2-week range kicked March S&Ps, which had been languishing slightly higher, to 767.00.

Most traders downplayed any glimmer of strength in March S&Ps. From the start of the day, traders attributed the contract's gains to an attempt to adjust its theoretical fair value to the cash market, rather than a directional move.
March S&Ps fell below fair value in the final minutes of Friday's pit session and closed at a discount to cash.
However, the contract's rallies were just as violent as the selloffs, and contributed to the steady rounds of arbitrage buy and sell programs, traders said.
"It's very easy for arbs to come in when you have two-point swings in less than two minutes," one trader said.
Arbitrage buy programs were seen at about a 5.40-point premium to cash, while arbitrage sell programs were cited at a 3.20-point premium.
On Monday, fair value stood at a premium between 3.50 and 3.70 points, traders said.

The lack of upside momentum in S&Ps and the Nasdaq 100 index did little to hoist Nikkei 225 futures off their lows. In fact, March Nikkeis widened losses to 17,185, a contract low, on concerns about the health of Japan's banking and financial sectors, traders said.
Despite March S&Ps' drop below the one-week low of 768.50 to the lowest level in nearly two weeks, many traders look for the market to advance in the intermediate term.
Further support is at the January 14 low of 763.35 and 762.00.
Traders said the direction of Tuesday's market will hinge on the U.S. fourth-quarter employment cost index, which is expected to rise 0.9 percent.

At the close of pit trade, March S&Ps were off 0.80 at 768.95, KCBT Value Lines were off 0.85 at 698.00, NYSE Composites were off 0.75 at 404.95, Nikkeis were down 280 at 17,220, Midcap 400s were 0.10 lower at 262.65 and Nasdaq 100s were down 5.75 at 897.75.
